findings.title: 20260811T040000Z.json finding missing from index.json findings array
findings.detail: The finding AUDIT-audit-elevation-day-counts-20260811 (status: fixed) appears in .audits/20260811T040000Z.json and is counted in fixed_this_run: 1, but is absent from the index.json findings array. The index is a complete rollup of all findings across all scans; every finding, whether open or fixed, should appear there for audit-trail completeness.
findings.fix_sketch: Add the 2026-08-11 finding entry to the findings array in index.json, preserving its status: fixed and all fields from the scan file.
findings.fix_summary: Added AUDIT-audit-elevation-day-counts-20260811 finding entry to index.json findings array with all fields from 20260811T040000Z.json.

findings.title: closing_pr: null in 20260811T040000Z.json — schema requires integer 0 for local-only fixes
findings.detail: The single finding in .audits/20260811T040000Z.json has closing_pr: null. Per self-heal-pipeline.md: 'If the closure landed without a PR (rare; only for local-only repos), use 0 and explain in fix_summary.' This is a recurring schema violation — the same issue was previously fixed for 20260802T080000Z.json as AUDIT-audit-elevation-03554cf4.
findings.fix_sketch: Change closing_pr from null to 0 in .audits/20260811T040000Z.json.
findings.fix_summary: Changed closing_pr from null to 0 in .audits/20260811T040000Z.json to conform to the schema.

findings.title: rubric_version '1.0' in 20260811T040000Z.json — rubric.json declares '1.0.0' (semver)
findings.detail: The scan file .audits/20260811T040000Z.json uses rubric_version: '1.0', but rubric.json declares rubric_version: '1.0.0'. The rubric is the single source of truth for this field. This is a scanner consistency issue — the value should exactly match the rubric.json declaration.
findings.fix_summary: Changed rubric_version from '1.0' to '1.0.0' in .audits/20260811T040000Z.json to match rubric.json declaration.

findings.title: Finding ID 'AUDIT-audit-elevation-day-counts-20260811' in 20260811T040000Z.json does not conform to 8-hex-chars schema
findings.detail: plan.md specifies the ID format as 'AUDIT-<repo>-<8hexchars>' where 8hexchars are the first 8 hex characters of the finding's fingerprint SHA256. The ID 'AUDIT-audit-elevation-day-counts-20260811' uses a descriptive suffix instead. Additionally, the stored fingerprint (e0b431d0...) matches an already-closed finding (AUDIT-audit-elevation-e0b431d0 from 2026-08-06), suggesting the scanner reused the previous finding's fingerprint instead of computing a fresh one for this finding's distinct title. This is a recurring issue — previously fixed for 20260703T050000Z.json as AUDIT-audit-elevation-3a02f6b1.
findings.fix_sketch: Cannot fix without recomputing the correct SHA256 fingerprint for this finding's distinct title. Left open — scanner must compute fresh fingerprints per rubric.json fingerprint_algo on each scan.

findings.title: ADR-0002 body contains self-referential cross-reference 'Docker-unreachable fallback in ADR-0002'
findings.detail: In docs/ifleet-integration-adrs.md, the Decision section of ADR-0002 reads: 'matches the Docker-unreachable fallback in ADR-0002'. Since this text appears inside ADR-0002 itself, a reader naturally interprets it as a circular reference. The intended reference is to IFleet's own internal ADR-0002 (at IFleet/docs/adr/). The ambiguity arises because this document and the IFleet repo both use an ADR-0002 label.
findings.fix_sketch: Qualify the reference to 'Docker-unreachable fallback in IFleet repo ADR-0002' to distinguish it from this document's ADR-0002.
findings.fix_summary: Qualified 'Docker-unreachable fallback in ADR-0002' to 'Docker-unreachable fallback in IFleet repo ADR-0002' in the ADR-0002 Decision section of docs/ifleet-integration-adrs.md.

findings.title: proposer-spec.md §3 pre-filter description misleadingly implies only COSMETIC findings are skipped when closed/fixed
findings.detail: The third sentence of the Pre-filter block reads: 'COSMETIC findings with status: "closed" or "fixed" are also skipped'. This is redundant with the first sentence ('drop any finding with status not in ["open", "regression"]') and misleadingly implies that CRITICAL and IMPORTANT findings with those statuses might NOT be skipped. The correct invariant is that ALL findings with status outside ["open", "regression"] are skipped regardless of severity.
findings.fix_sketch: Remove or reword the redundant third sentence to eliminate the misleading severity qualifier.
findings.fix_summary: Replaced 'COSMETIC findings with status: "closed" or "fixed" are also skipped' with 'Findings with any other status (closed, fixed, verifying, fixing) are also excluded — the first sentence's rule applies to all severities equally.'
